reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports all key premises with specific experimental and DFT results for an N–Pt/HEA/C catalyst, though the evidence is from electrocatalytic ORR conditions, not automotive exhaust with H2O and NO, which is a minor overstatement of direct applicability.
premises: A Pt-rich shell on a high-entropy alloy adjusts adsorption energies of *O and *OH, reducing OH poisoning and enhancing ORR activity.
N-doping further regulates intermediate binding strength, boosting ORR activity and stability.
Multiple M–N bonds (e.g., Ni–N, Co–N) suppress dissolution/oxidation of transition metals.
N-doping optimizes the electronic structure of surface Pt, inhibiting Pt shell dissolution.
The combined effect of high entropy, M–N bonds, and a Pt-rich shell yields excellent long-term durability under HDV conditions.
